title: Module quiz: Distributing tools across agents

questions.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. The tool that closes a customer's account carries a description that warns the model to use it carefully. What should actually limit it?

options.text: A longer warning in the description, with an example of when to avoid it
options.says: Ruled out because "an instruction not to use a tool is a request".

options.text: A required parameter in which the model gives its reason for calling
options.says: Ruled out because a field in which the model states its reason "is a claim by the model, not a check".

options.text: A prompt rule that forbids the call unless the customer asks for it
options.says: Ruled out because a prompt rule is still "an instruction not to use a tool", and "an instruction not to use a tool is a request".

options.text: Authorisation and scope enforced in code, whatever the caller asks
options.says: A limit that the model cannot talk its way around lives in code.

questions.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. Refunds cannot be undone, the policy cap is 500, and every refund needs a person's approval. A call for 450 arrives and nobody has approved it. What should the tool layer return?

options.text: A result that runs the refund and logs that the amount is under the cap
options.says: Ruled out because "An irreversible call needs an approval even when the amount is under the cap".

options.text: A result that runs the refund and notifies a person to review it afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because "a review after the fact cannot undo an irreversible call".

options.text: A flagged refusal that waits for a human sign-off on this very request
options.says: An irreversible call waits for a person even under the cap.

options.text: A flagged refusal that sends the case to a person who can raise the cap
options.says: Ruled out because the route to a person who can raise the limit is for an amount above the cap: "An amount above the cap is refused and sent to a person", and 450 is under 500.

origin.section: Caps and authorisation on irreversible tools

questions.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator delegates to a web search subagent, a document analysis subagent and a synthesis subagent, and it produces a cited report. All subagents hold the same 18 tools, including the one that sends the finished report, and the synthesis subagent has begun running web searches. Which redesign fits best?

options.text: Split the list by role, and give the irreversible step one owner behind an approval
options.says: Scoped lists remove the misuse, and the irreversible step has an owner and an approval.

options.text: Keep one list and add a prompt line for each role naming the tools to use
options.says: Ruled out because a prompt line is a request: "an instruction not to use a tool is a request, and a tool the agent holds is a tool it can use".

options.text: Cut the shared list to the ten most used tools and keep it the same for every role
options.says: Ruled out because "an agent outside its specialisation misuses what it holds".

options.text: Route each request through a classifier that enables a subset of the tools
options.says: Ruled out because "a router adds a component to keep correct".
